title: Band concerts at Altamont Park; the only Black classical cornet soloist
summary: He played in park band concerts in Steubenville, memorising classical solos by Herbert Clarke, and says he was the only Black player of that kind.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: No, he wasn't particular about you learning things. I tell you, I used to play at the band concert, Alamont Park. In Steubensville, Ohio.
You played in band concerts, this was classical band music?
No, just get in the park and tell you to play this down. You didn't have a chance to do anything with it.
Was this an all black group or was it a mixed group?
Mixed.
Black, White, black, everybody.
Italians mostly.
Now, oh, yeah, that's another thing. I had an Italian teacher, oh, yeah, I forgot that. Those things go out of your mind, Buddy.
then-- What kind of material were you playing at some of those classical solos?
Classical.
Something like Herbie Clark type solo.
How did you remember that? How did you think of that? Herbie Clark. You sure know -- yeah, I played a lot of Herbert Clark stuff, a lot of that.
At that point, were there a lot of black trumpet players? There couldn't have been too many playing classical music.
No, they didn't, not too many.
There was a problem of
Finding teachers like that.
I was the only one.
You were probably the only one at that point, because most of them didn't have good teachers. You were probably the first.
Yes, I was and I was on the outside of the band.
What do you mean, when the band
Yeah, I was out front playing.
You had memorized those solos.
Memorized solos and so forth.
That's really tough.
That's been a long time ago, let's get off of that.
Well, we got to know about these little periods.
I can't remember all them things.
